proof_status: complete written arguments with explicit external theorem inputs
internal_checks: Checked canonical uniqueness, gcd normalization, signed common-neighbor recovery, rational reconstruction and the binary dyadic bounds.
Checked signed fixed-edge counting for real and imaginary quadratic fields, split and irreducible binomials, and the irreducibility of the mixed affine cubics.
Checked both height-loss branches and the argument for the smallest canonical box in the primitive-triple bound, allowing either sign of its deviation from 1/(k+1).

Tested the primitive-triple box inequalities in exact arithmetic on 4,509,321 rational-grid and targeted triples, including both height-loss branches. The written argument proves the unrestricted inequalities.
Checked mixed signed common-neighbor recovery, the fixed-edge reduction to degree gcd(e,f), the three explicit mixed savings and both congruence progressions.
Tested mixed elimination exactly for both signs, checked the two residue periods, and exercised the three bounds on 20,480 rational mixed boxes.
Checked the hypotheses and exponents of Browning–Verzobio Theorem 1.2, the height margin for gcd at least two, and the small-coordinate alternatives with explicit error scales.
Verified all consecutive-case cost certificates and the even-residue obstruction in exact rational arithmetic.
Checked omitted-product grouping in the signed coefficient form, including per-prime minimum valuation and recovery of the non-omitted coordinates.
Checked 19,157 grouped canonical valuation cases and verified the even-residue rational certificates and the grouped height-loss branch.

Checked the surface-only moment bounds at all offsets, the aligned graph inequalities including all four small-coordinate cases, and families attaining the surface-only constants in the normalized model for u>v.
Verified the first fixed-offset obstruction in exact arithmetic for both representatives modulo 60 of r congruent to 2 modulo 30, with a symbolic gcd proof for the entire progression.
Generated an exact branch certificate for (u,v,r)=(2,1,60) and a rational witness for (3,1,62). The standard-library verifier accepted both and rejected corrupted copies.
Checked cancellation-free pair amplification, powerful divisor selection, and the archimedean and modular determinant bounds in the uniform monomial proof.

Checked four generalized Vandermonde identities and multi-prime valuation examples exactly. The small prime-power scan covered 48 boxes and had no genuinely modular collisions; it is diagnostic rather than proof.

Checked the 90/10 perturbation, all compatible graph bounds and the strict maximum-sum inequality in exact arithmetic, and proved simultaneous cardinality and codegree bounds for the abstract tripartite construction.
Checked both signs of the coefficient-uniform quadratic count, grouped root recovery, the parity cost inequality, and the moment normalization and height errors for all even-power coordinates.
Proved the 8/3 cost bound by grouping indices 0 and 2 and treating every pattern of unavailable arcs; replayed a separate exact 21-node certificate.

For orders divisible by six, replayed an exact certificate for cost at least 4 with 293 splits, 790 dual leaves and 69 infeasible leaves. Checked transfer of finite branch certificates under O(k^(-1/2)) perturbations. The checker rejected an increased threshold and an invalid residue class.
Reduced the two-exponent product congruence to the existing modular quotient theorem by inversion and relabeling, retaining both unequal height bounds.

Checked weighted representation-pair recovery for both signs, including identical retained tuples and the degenerate exact rational equality. The diagonal representation pairs are counted once in the second moment.
Checked the truncated moment identity for D at least 5. Replayed both exact parity certificates and checked the finite multiplier transfer to errors of order k^(-1/10).
The standalone checker rejected both certificates after increasing their target cost. It accepted the earlier even-order certificate after the checker extension.
Scanned 24 small prime-power boxes. The 118240 ratio pairs had 116 non-singleton fibers, all arising from exact rational equalities. The scan is diagnostic.
Checked the two height-dependent conditions in the general determinant proof after replacing the upper height by n^(C/r) for every fixed C.
Checked prime-exponent division, coprimality and injectivity for the direct compression T=R(a)/R(b), V=W(a)/W(b). Ran 700 exact coprime compression cases and 1005 integer parameter checks.

Checked the rectangular determinant, the Taylor stability threshold and the capped-divisor construction after discarding a bounded product of small prime powers. Ran 28 exact local determinant checks and five prime-power or composite divisor checks.
Checked the product-of-coordinates counting threshold, the summation over k-full targets and the fixed-offset transfer by monotonicity.
Checked the full determinant divisibility via expansion in comparison and error rows, including when the total Vandermonde valuation exceeds the available congruence precision.
Checked the selected-prime average starting from twice the matrix dimension, the pruning threshold, and the entrywise precision loss under the triangular Newton transform.

Checked stability of the comparison determinant at the selected prime and verified the height slack required when the modulus c is below X. Ran 37 exact local determinant tests and 1005 integer parameter checks.

Checked the subset exchange argument, weighted prime average, and the effect of the bounded deeper modulus and discarded prime powers. Ran 125 exact exchange diagnostics and seven prime-adic examples approaching the exchange constant.
Checked the determinant divisibility including error rows, the Newton precision after selecting the minimizing subset, the modulus floors and the dyadic transfer without additional height slack.

Replayed the exact inequalities for the proposed 1/320, the improved c-based 1/300 and the adaptive-target 1/153 parameter choices. Verified the initial-row optimization and the finite prime-power height ceiling calculation.
Checked the three dyadic cases when the target is chosen by residual-factor size, including the extra saving from a small exceptional target. Ran 3396 exact signed adaptive-target compression tests.
Built the standalone LaTeX source, checked diagnostics, and rendered and visually inspected all twenty-two PDF pages.

modular_monomials.unit_condition: numerators, denominators and K coprime to n
modular_monomials.exponents: distinct e,f in [r,r+A] with A fixed
modular_monomials.height_range: n^(1/(3r)) <= Y <= n^(C/r), for any fixed C >= 2

even_diagonal.saving: 8/(3k^2) + O(k^(-5/2)) for all sufficiently large even k
even_diagonal.saving_divisible_by_six: 4/k^2 + O(k^(-5/2)) for all sufficiently large multiples of six

direct_compression.diagonal_saving: (1/512000) k^(-3/2) for all sufficiently large k
direct_compression.fixed_offsets_saving: (1/1024000) r^(-3/2) for all sufficiently large r in terms of the offsets
direct_compression.modular_lemma: For k-full n, h=floor(sqrt(k)/2000), H(T)<=n^(2/k), H(V)<=n^(h/(64k)): O_(k,epsilon)(n^(1/(4k)+epsilon)) unit rational pairs with V T^k=K modulo n.

divided_differences.fixed_offsets_saving: 2^(-17)/r for all sufficiently large r in terms of the offsets
divided_differences.modular_lemma: For k-full n, delta=2^(-16), lambda=65/64, H(T)<=n^(lambda/k), H(V)<=n^(lambda*delta): O_(k,epsilon)(n^(1/(2k)+epsilon)) positive unit rational pairs with V T^k=K modulo n.

adaptive_determinant.fixed_offsets_saving: 1/(306r) for all sufficiently large r in terms of the offsets
adaptive_determinant.modular_lemma: For each modular profile and k-full n, count positive rational unit pairs with H(T)<=n^(theta/k), H(V)<=n^(residual_height) and V T^k=K modulo n by O_(k,epsilon)(n^((1-saving)/k+epsilon)), uniformly in K.
